Next 16 collects page data with NODE_ENV=production, firing two pre-existing module-scope fail-closed guards (src/lib/paymongo.ts:39 from 05-02, and the Inngest signing-key guard).

blockers.description: Verification blind spot, no owner assigned. The local `public` schema was three migrations behind (0010-0012, Phase 6) and nothing caught it. tests/helpers/db.ts replays migrations into isolated per-test schemas, so a stale `public` schema is invisible to the entire suite. Phase 6 verified green against a DB that never had its own booking_no_overlap widening applied.
blockers.workaround: Run `npm run db:migrate` and confirm nothing pending before trusting any phase verification. A pre-phase guard asserting `public` is fully migrated is the real fix.

decisions.decision: Executed all 15 plans sequentially rather than in parallel worktrees
decisions.rationale: workflow.use_worktrees is false in .planning/config.json; concurrent commits on one working tree would interleave. The one time two agents ran concurrently (07-01 + 07-02) it required manual arbitration of STATE.md ownership — evidence the sequential default is right here.

decisions.decision: Orchestrator applied migrations 0013/0014 directly rather than re-dispatching 07-01 blind
decisions.rationale: Docker recovered mid-session; applying and snapshotting booking_no_overlap before/after gave a byte-level diff proving the D-21 keystone was untouched.

decisions.decision: 07-01 was allowed to repair two call sites outside its files_modified (payout-sweep.ts ON CONFLICT target, request-lifecycle.test.ts stale 24h assertion)
decisions.rationale: Both breakages were causally its own schema/constant changes. A plan must not leave the tree red for a later wave to inherit.

decisions.decision: 07-02's Self-Check was flipped FAILED -> PASSED by the orchestrator with an evidence addendum
decisions.rationale: It was marked FAILED only because the DB was down when it ran. The owed gate was later executed and passed; the flip is documented in the SUMMARY with its evidence rather than silently rewritten.

decisions.decision: Recompute-wins for the refund preview/confirm gap (07-09)
decisions.rationale: There is no signed quote token, so honouring the page's number means trusting a client-transported figure. Time only moves toward the session, so a crossed boundary can only lower the refund. The review page discloses the concrete boundary so the recompute is disclosed, not sprung.

decisions.decision: NULL-tier listings disclose NOTHING rather than tierOrDefault's Flexible (07-15)
decisions.rationale: The fallback is an internal safety net so the refund engine never faces an unpriceable legacy row — it is not a policy any host chose. It is also safe in the only direction that matters: the fallback a booker would actually receive is the most generous rung.

decisions.decision: Reminder reachability is guarded by `deadline - OFFSET >= created_at`, not by `expires_at > now()` (07-13)
decisions.rationale: The plan, 07-RESEARCH Pitfall 9 and the orchestrator's brief all wrongly credited `> now()` with producing a no-send. A request 4h out gets a ~2h SLA, and now()+2h satisfies both `> now()` and `<= now()+6h`, so a range-only query fires a '6 hours left' reminder at creation time.

context_notes: Phase 7 executed 15/16 plans across 5 waves. All self-checks PASSED, working tree clean, full suite 76 files / 628 tests green, migrations 0013-0015 applied and idempotent, booking_no_overlap verified byte-for-byte intact. The value of this run was concentrated in defects a green suite could not see: NO REFUND COULD EVER HAVE BEEN DISPATCHED (booking.payment_method did not exist and isApiRefundable fails closed, so the 'createRefund called at most once' test passed vacuously with zero calls); a host could cancel another host's booking, refunding platform money and charging them a fee, because the plan's SQL omitted the host-ownership predicate; three money-flow bugs sat in 07-04's own plan text, including netting applied before a branch that DELETEs the claim; an unscoped ledger query in webhook handleRefund would have silently forgiven a host's cancellation debt; timestamptz came back as TEXT through an `as unknown as` cast that passed tsc, eslint AND next build and would have crashed on the first real row. The pattern worth carrying forward: plan text and research documents are FALLIBLE, and the executors that found the most were the ones that probed the live DB or mutation-tested a guard instead of trusting a documented claim. 07-13 disproved an assumption held simultaneously by its plan, by 07-RESEARCH and by the orchestrator.
